prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input roles: Image 1 is the current restored PNG to edit; Image 2 is the authoritative original painted pattern enlarged for inspection. Reconstruct only the emblem's original marks, preserving the original animal pose, facing direction, number, asymmetry, disconnected pieces and negative spaces. Correct obvious reconstruction drift from Image 2 without redesigning the emblem.
Primary request: redraw this emblem as a genuine ONE-INK illustration. Use only the specified single solid ink color and actual transparency. There is no second outline color, no black border unless black is the chosen ink, no white paint, gray shading, gradient, glow or drop shadow. All outlines, fills and sparse hatch strokes use the exact same ink. Interior light marks are transparent cutouts, not lighter paint and not opacity gradients.
Represent existing dark/light modeling through the distribution of the one ink: solid dark masses, clear transparent highlight slots, a few short widely spaced parallel hatch strokes within broad original painted regions where necessary. Keep large clear silhouettes. Use fewer, coarser marks rather than dense texture so this remains readable at a small 37 mm emblem size. Do not add ornaments, fur, scales or fabricated anatomy. Do not insert shading into areas that were unpainted stone: those areas stay transparent.
Style: crisp smooth flat 2D animation emblem / one-color print artwork. Preserve the recognizable original drawing, not a generic replacement. Restore the talisman art plane to a straight-on flat view while keeping the animal's original side/front pose.
Output: one centered independent transparent RGBA PNG, square 1024x1024 with roughly 80% maximum content extent and generous clear margins. No plaque, stone, octagon, rim, background, checkerboard pixels, text, extra subject or new decoration.
Ink color: #9B594B. Every visible ink mark uses this SAME color.
Animal-specific fidelity and one-ink instructions: ONE seated/coiled BROWN monkey. The left long tail curls into the original tight upper-left spiral and bottom U; right upper head and bent limbs keep their source separation and central transparent space. Correct the target's overly broad tail/body bands toward the slender source shapes. Use brown silhouette/contour and only a few transparent highlight cuts inside original broad strokes to suggest surface turn; never fill the entire body, invent fingers, eyes, fur or a second animal.
Flat vector-like solid screen-print ink; ALL interior filled regions must be perfectly uniform, no rendering noise, no internal lighting gradients. Transparency cuts must preserve source details; do not invent anatomy. Anti-aliasing only at shape edges.
visual_observation: Preserves the large upper-left spiral and lower U tail, right-side head/limb marks, and broad central negative space. Some curved marks remain broad and parallel; parent review needed.
